title: Authorization policy set
description: The authorization audit substrate defined in The Software Field Guide, issue #59: a subject registry, a non-overlapping rule history (versions), the version that answers today, and probes that pin the expected answers. This schema mirrors the shape rules of the Rego validator (policies/authz); the validator additionally enforces the semantic rules a JSON schema cannot — version windows must not overlap, rule ids unique per version, subject ids unique, the current version must exist and be in effect, and every probe's expectation must survive a replay against the current version.

currentVersion.description: The version that answers requests today. Explicit, never derived from the clock. Must name a declared version that is in effect on the validation date.

disabled.description: Kill switch. A disabled policy set denies every request by construction (rule policy/disabled-fail-closed).

subjects.description: Subject registry: who can appear in a rule. Roles say what a subject is; flags say what state a subject is in.

id.description: Subject id. Must be unique across the registry.

roles.description: What the subject is, e.g. checkout-clerk.

flags.description: What state the subject is in, e.g. mfa-verified, offboarded.

versions.description: Rule history. Version numbers are unique; effective windows must not overlap; the current version carries forward the rules that still hold.

version.description: Version number. Unique across the set.

effectiveFrom.description: First day the version is in effect, YYYY-MM-DD.

effectiveTo.description: Last day the version is in effect, YYYY-MM-DD. Omitted on the newest version means 'in force until superseded'. Must not precede effectiveFrom.

rules.description: The rules in force in this version.

probes.description: Requests the current version must answer as promised. They make the set self-testing in CI and are the inventory the disabled-state check proves fail-closed with.

subject.description: Subject id, resolved against the registry.

context.description: Request context, e.g. {"mfa": true}. Values are scalars (string, number, boolean).

expect.description: The answer the current version must give. The validator replays every probe and flags any mismatch.

selector.description: Names exactly one subject criterion: a registry id, a role, or a flag.

id.description: Rule id. Unique within a version; the same id across versions means 'the same rule, still in force'.

description.description: Why the rule exists, in one sentence.

effect.description: What the rule does when every criterion matches. A matching deny beats every matching allow.

action.description: An exact action, or a trailing-* pattern (order.*, or * for any). Wildcards are trailing-only.

resource.description: An exact resource, or a trailing-* pattern (orders-*, or * for any). Wildcards are trailing-only.

condition.description: Context fields that must all equal the expected values for the rule to match, e.g. {"mfa": true}. Equality on scalars only.
